summary: Import-time AES-decrypt-and-eval of hidden payload in claimed color-gradient library
details: uzair-rajput-new@1.3.0 ships CommonJS and ESM entrypoints (dist/index.cjs, dist/index.js) that contain a large base64 literal which is AES-256-CBC decrypted at require() time using a hardcoded password ('meRijan2feb') and salt ('uzair-rajput-salt-2024'), then executed via `new Function('module','exports','require','__dirname','__filename', <decrypted>)` with the module's own module/exports/require passed in. The decrypted body (~12 KB) runs with full ambient privilege on import. Three sibling modules (dist/_a.cjs, dist/_b.cjs, dist/_c.cjs) export short byte arrays and are require()'d but not referenced by the visible loader path, consistent with additional concealed material. The package advertises itself as a terminal color-gradient library — a category whose functionality (see the widely used gradient-string) is a few hundred lines of plain JavaScript with no need for encrypted, dynamically evaluated source. The actual behavior of the executed payload is not inspectable from source; anything from credential theft to a backdoor runs in the installer's process on import with no visible code path.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
